proposals.claim: High-rise trousers paired with front-tucked boxy tops create visual elongation and proportion balance for varied body types
proposals.rationale: Front tucks on boxy tops when combined with high-rise waistbands establish a defined waistline and create vertical sightlines that counterbalance wider silhouettes, while distributing fabric strategically
constraints: Tuck depth and placement must be tested on intended wearer silhouettes
Fabric weight compatibility between top and trouser required to avoid bulk at tuck point
Top length must clear hip points to avoid unflattering bunching
evidenceNeeded: Fit testing across 3+ body type categories
Photographic documentation of tuck stability throughout wear
Feedback on visual proportion perception from diverse wearers

proposals.claim: Korean-style wide-leg trousers with structured boxy crop-length tops create balanced proportions and contemporary silhouette
proposals.rationale: Korean wide trousers with relaxed inseam and high rise pair effectively with shorter boxy cuts to avoid overwhelming the upper body; the cropped length prevents visual heaviness while maintaining proportional balance
constraints: Inseam measurement must account for regional sizing variations
Boxy top length must be tested to ensure it doesn't create bottom-heavy visual weight
Trouser rise compatibility with undergarment visibility requires validation
evidenceNeeded: Measurement specifications for Korean trouser width standards
Proportion studies comparing top length to trouser volume
Wearer feedback on mobility and comfort in cropped/wide combinations

proposals.claim: Limit patterned cross-garment combinations to single focal pattern plus solid anchors to prevent visual noise and maintain design coherence
proposals.rationale: Pairing two or more competing patterns across upper and lower body creates visual fragmentation; strategic use of one printed/textured piece with solid partners maintains design hierarchy and wearer focus
constraints: Pattern scale, color saturation, and frequency must be defined per combination
Solid piece selection requires consideration of pattern color pulls and undertones
Context of wear (casual vs. formal) impacts pattern appropriateness thresholds
evidenceNeeded: Visual coherence assessments from design professionals
Wearer comfort/confidence feedback on pattern combinations
Documentation of pattern scale relationships and color interaction

proposals.claim: Cross-garment formality requires intentional matching of fabric refinement and construction detail between top and bottom pieces to maintain cohesive dresscode compliance
proposals.rationale: Mixing formal tailoring (sharp creases, premium fabric) on trousers with casual construction (soft drape, relaxed seaming) on tops creates visual contradiction; formality perception depends on consistent signal across both garments
constraints: Fabric hand and finish must be comparable between pieces
Seam construction detail visibility impacts perceived formality level
Occasion context determines formality standards and acceptable mixing
evidenceNeeded: Professional assessment of formality consistency across garment pairs
Feedback from appropriate social/workplace contexts on dresscode perception
Documentation of construction details influencing formality read

proposals.claim: Cross-garment climate appropriateness requires testing sleeve length, fabric weight, and neckline combinations to ensure functional layering capacity and temperature regulation
proposals.rationale: Boxy tops with high-rise trousers must accommodate climate-appropriate layering; sleeve length affects jacket integration, fabric weight impacts insulation needs, and neckline determines base-layer visibility and weather protection
constraints: Regional climate data must inform fiber content and weight recommendations
Sleeve length must be tested with intended outer-layer dimensions
Neckline height impacts thermal protection and layering versatility
evidenceNeeded: Thermal comfort testing across seasonal temperature ranges
Layering compatibility trials with standard outerwear pieces
Wearer feedback on climate adaptation functionality

proposals.claim: Wide-leg trouser volume must be balanced by structured top silhouettes; cropped boxy tops reduce visual weight distribution more effectively than standard-length pieces
proposals.rationale: Volume concentration at lower body requires visual weight mitigation at upper body; boxy crop-length tops interrupt the vertical sightline and create horizontal emphasis that counterbalances wide trouser legs, whereas longer tops extend downward volume
constraints: Body height and proportional measurements affect ideal crop length
Top structure and seaming impact visual weight perception
Trouser inseam length interacts with top length ratio in proportion equation
evidenceNeeded: Proportion analysis across height ranges (petite, average, tall)
Side-by-side visual documentation of different top lengths with same trouser
Wearer feedback on silhouette perception and confidence

proposals.claim: Boxy top shoulder width and neckline treatment must align with trouser waistline visual weight to maintain upper-lower body proportion harmony
proposals.rationale: Oversized or exaggerated shoulder treatment on boxy tops can overpower high-rise waistbands if neckline creates excessive width; coherent shoulder-to-hip visual flow depends on intentional relationship between these three anchor points
constraints: Shoulder seam placement must be documented and tested
Neckline width perception interacts with face shape and frame size
Waistband prominence and color affect perception of shoulder-hip balance
evidenceNeeded: Measurement documentation of shoulder width relative to waistband width
Visual studies comparing different neckline treatments with same trouser
Diverse wearer feedback on upper-lower body coherence and balance

proposals.claim: Combining complementary fabric textures (structured on top, smooth on bottom or vice versa) creates cross-garment visual interest without pattern conflict
proposals.rationale: When pattern-loading is constrained, strategic texture pairing (e.g., textured linen boxy top with smooth cotton sateen wide trousers) provides design dimension and tactile interest while maintaining visual simplicity and formality coherence
constraints: Texture must not conflict with stated formality level or occasion context
Fabric texture interaction with lighting and body movement requires documentation
Care and durability of mixed-texture combinations must be verified
evidenceNeeded: Documentation of texture combinations and visual effect across lighting conditions
Wearer feedback on perceived sophistication and design coherence
Durability and maintenance testing of recommended texture pairings
